common_sections.title: Executive Summary
common_sections.description: High-level overview of the analysis scope, key findings, and strategic recommendations
common_sections.content_guidance: 2-3 paragraph summary covering: what was analyzed, top 3-5 key findings, and primary strategic recommendation

common_sections.title: Market Context
common_sections.description: Global and local market landscape relevant to the analysis
common_sections.content_guidance: Industry Overview: 1-2 explained paragraphs, not a single line. Market Size & Growth: 4-5 detailed, explained points covering market size, growth rate, segment breakdowns, and the specific drivers behind the numbers — each point 1-2 sentences. A precise number (market size, CAGR, growth rate) may ONLY appear when the evidence actually contains it with a citable source; where the evidence has no such figure, describe the market's scale and trajectory qualitatively instead of stating an unsourced precise number — '4-5 points' means 4-5 substantive points, not 4-5 invented statistics. Key Trends & Drivers: 4-5 trends, each stated and then explained (what it is, why it matters, what evidence supports it), not a labeled one-liner. Use tables for comparative data where helpful.

common_sections.title: Consumer Landscape
common_sections.description: Target audience analysis, behavior patterns, and consumer insights
common_sections.content_guidance: Target Segments: define 4-5 key consumer segments; for each, explain its distinct needs and behaviours in 1-2 sentences, grounded in the research where it provides evidence for that segment rather than a generic persona label. Consumer Behavior: 4-5 detailed, explained behavioural points, each grounded in research evidence or clearly-reasoned market context, not a bare one-line label. Perception & Sentiment: explain both the positive and negative sides of perception in 2-4 sentences, citing specific evidence (ratings, named reviews/incidents) where the research supports it rather than a single generic statement.

common_sections.title: Competitive Landscape
common_sections.content_guidance: Key Competitors: identify 4-6 key competitors; for EACH, write a short profile (2-3 sentences) covering its market positioning, one notable strength, and one notable fact drawn from its own research — not a single one-line label. Competitive Analysis: use a comparison TABLE, but make each Strengths/Weaknesses entry specific and evidence-grounded (cite a fact, rating, or incident from that competitor's own research where available), not a generic phrase. Market Positioning: a full paragraph (4-6 sentences) explaining how the competitive set is positioned relative to each other and to the target brand — not a single summary line.

common_sections.title: Key Insights
common_sections.description: Synthesized insights from market, consumer, and competitive analysis
common_sections.content_guidance: Consumer Insights: 4-5 detailed insights, each framed as an observation (grounded in the Consumer Landscape analysis above) followed by its strategic implication, in 1-2 sentences each — not a bare label. Market & Competitive Insights: 4-5 detailed insights in the same observation-then-implication format, each grounded in the Market Context, Competitive Landscape, or Brand Audit analysis above.

type_specific_sections.title: Brand Audit
type_specific_sections.description: A direct, evidence-based audit of the TARGET brand itself — its own strengths and, separately, its own weaknesses and vulnerabilities. This is not a competitor comparison (that belongs in Competitive Landscape) and not aspirational positioning (that belongs in Strategic Approach / Positioning Map) — it is a candid look at the brand as the research actually describes it.
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: The risk and depth research for the TARGET brand is provided in FULL below (not a sample). Before writing Weaknesses & Vulnerabilities, check the evidence against EACH of these categories separately, in this order, and give EVERY category that has a documented issue its OWN bullet — do not merge two or more categories into one combined/vague bullet: (1) customer rating/review-platform evidence (name the platform and the exact rating/score, e.g. 'rated 1.4/5 on Trustpilot'); (2) delivery/timeline issues (name the specific project AND the specific delay duration or date, e.g. 'a 7-year delay on The Views'); (3) legal, regulatory, or litigation matters (name the specific matter, e.g. 'an FIR for forgery filed against the MD'); (4) financial-distress figures — treat EVERY distinct financial metric as its own sub-item, not just whichever one you mention first: check separately for (4a) a net-worth or total-liabilities figure, (4b) a debt-service coverage ratio (DSCR) or any other named coverage/leverage ratio, (4c) a borrowings/debt figure, (4d) a credit-rating status. If the evidence contains more than one of these, give EACH its own bullet — e.g. 'negative net worth of roughly Rs 2,929 crore' is one bullet and, separately, 'a DSCR of 0.21' is another bullet; citing only the net-worth figure and silently dropping a DSCR or borrowings figure that IS in the evidence is incomplete and not acceptable; (5) any other distinct named incident the evidence documents. Skip a category only if the evidence genuinely has nothing in it — never skip one that has a fact just to keep the list short, and never combine two categories' facts (or two distinct figures within the same category) into a single line ('legal and financial challenges' is NOT acceptable when the evidence names a specific FIR and a specific net-worth figure — those are two separate bullets). For Strengths, similarly list every genuine strength the evidence or research context actually supports. Do not pad with generic filler, and do not invent a rating, date, figure, or incident the evidence does not contain — if a category genuinely has nothing specific, state it generally or omit that category. Cite each specific figure per the source-citation rule.

type_specific_sections.title: Strategic Approach
type_specific_sections.description: Recommended strategic direction and positioning options
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Present 3-5 strategic options, each explained in 1-2 sentences covering what it is AND its key trade-off. Recommend one with clear, evidence-grounded rationale (2-4 sentences).

type_specific_sections.title: Positioning Map
type_specific_sections.description: Visual positioning analysis showing brand placement vs competitors
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Define 2 key positioning axes most relevant given the research (prefer an axis the evidence can actually support, such as Trust or Quality, when documented evidence exists for it, over a vaguer label chosen to avoid grounding). Describe where the brand and each competitor sits on both axes with brief grounded reasoning, not just coordinates. Identify 2-3 white-space opportunities, each explained in 1-2 sentences. Reference a positioning map chart.

type_specific_sections.title: Strategy Build
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Include a clear positioning statement. Build a messaging hierarchy of 3-4 pillars, each with its core message, 1-2 proof points drawn from the research where available, and target audience. Outline 3-4 content pillars and channel recommendations, each with a brief (1-2 sentence) rationale for why it fits this brand's specific situation, not a generic channel list.

type_specific_sections.title: Measurement & Roadmap
type_specific_sections.description: KPIs, implementation timeline, and risk assessment
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Define 5-8 measurable KPIs in a TABLE. Create a 3-phase roadmap (30/60/90 days or Q1/Q2/Q3), each phase with 2-3 explained actions, not just a label. Include budget ranges. Risk Assessment should name 3-5 top risks — where the research documents a specific risk for this brand (a delivery, regulatory, or financial issue), name it specifically rather than only listing generic macro/industry risks.

type_specific_sections.title: Competitor Deep Dive
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Detailed profile per competitor in TABLE format. SWOT for top 3. Identify sustainable competitive advantages.

type_specific_sections.title: Competitive Strategy
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Map differentiation opportunities. Outline response strategies for competitive threats.

type_specific_sections.title: Action Plan & Recommendations
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Prioritized action items in TABLE. 90-day timeline. Define measurable success metrics.

type_specific_sections.title: Technical SEO Analysis
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Include technical metrics in TABLEs. Score each area. Identify critical technical issues.

type_specific_sections.title: Content & On-Page SEO
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Keyword opportunity TABLE. Content gaps vs competitors. Page-level optimization recommendations.

type_specific_sections.title: Off-Page & Authority
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Backlink metrics in TABLE. Authority comparison vs competitors. Prioritized link building tactics.

type_specific_sections.title: SEO Roadmap & KPIs
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Categorize actions by timeline. Define ranking and traffic KPIs in TABLE.

type_specific_sections.title: Platform Strategy & Content Pillars
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Rank 3-4 priority platforms with rationale. Define 4-5 content pillars with example formats. Establish brand voice guardrails.

type_specific_sections.title: Content Calendar Framework
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Define posting frequency per platform in a TABLE. Specify a content mix ratio (e.g. 40% educational / 30% promotional / 30% engagement). Flag upcoming seasonal moments to tie into.

type_specific_sections.title: Engagement & Community Growth
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Outline response-time SLAs and engagement tactics. Identify UGC/influencer collaboration opportunities. List 3-5 organic growth tactics.

type_specific_sections.title: Measurement & Optimization
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Define KPIs per platform (reach, engagement rate, follower growth, conversion) in a TABLE. Propose an A/B testing roadmap for content formats.

type_specific_sections.title: Market Readiness Assessment
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Assess regulatory/compliance requirements for the target market. Identify localization needs (language, payment methods, cultural fit). Score entry barriers (High/Med/Low) with rationale.

type_specific_sections.title: Entry Model & Go-To-Market Approach
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Compare entry modes (direct, partnership, franchise, acquisition) in a TABLE. Recommend one with rationale. Identify potential local partners/channels.

type_specific_sections.title: Localized Positioning & Pricing
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Map local competitors. Recommend price positioning relative to the local market (adjusted for local purchasing power). Flag messaging/cultural adaptations needed.

type_specific_sections.title: Entry Roadmap & Risk Plan
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: 90/180/365-day phased entry plan in a TABLE. Estimate investment ranges per phase. Identify the top 3-5 market entry risks with mitigation.

type_specific_sections.title: Content Pillars & Themes
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Define 4-5 content pillars tied to brand goals. Map upcoming seasonal/cultural moments relevant to the brand. Recommend a format mix (video/carousel/static/blog).

type_specific_sections.title: Editorial Calendar
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Produce a 30-day content grid TABLE (Date, Platform, Pillar, Format, Caption Hook). Note platform-specific adaptations. Specify publishing frequency per channel.

type_specific_sections.title: Production Workflow & Resourcing
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Outline the content pipeline from ideation to publish. Define an approval workflow with turnaround SLAs. Flag resourcing/tooling gaps.

type_specific_sections.title: Performance Tracking
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Define per-format KPIs in a TABLE. Set a cadence for reviewing top/bottom performing content. Outline how insights feed back into the next cycle.

type_specific_sections.title: Detailed Analysis
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Deep dive into the analysis topic. Use TABLEs for data comparison.

type_specific_sections.title: Strategic Recommendations
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: 3-5 prioritized recommendations. Each with rationale, effort level, and expected impact.

type_specific_sections.title: Next Steps & Measurement
type_specific_sections.content_guidance: Actionable next steps in TABLE format. Define measurable outcomes.
